basic_identification.full_title: Unplasticized PVC Pipes for Water Supplies — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard covers the requirements for plain as well as socket-ended unplasticized polyvinyl chloride (UPVC) pipes, including those designed for use with elastomeric sealing rings, intended for potable water supplies and agricultural use. It explicitly excludes UPVC pipes used in suction and delivery lines of agricultural pumps (which are covered under IS 12231) and screen/casing pipes utilized in tube wells (which are governed by IS 12818).

certification_and_marking.disclaimer: No mandatory BIS product certification (such as the ISI Mark) is strictly required within the code of practice text itself for purchasing or installing the pipes. However, to guarantee conformity and safe usage, the standard establishes the following voluntary BIS Standard Mark scheme alongside critical material-level, physical, chemical, and test certification requirements:

requirements.provision: The product conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, and marked with the Standard Mark.
Base resin K-value (minimum 64) and VCM content limit conformances must be backed by a test report or conformity certificate from the resin manufacturer once every three months.
Rubber joint seals must comply with IS 5382, supported by a conformity certificate from the gasket manufacturer once every three months.

Pipes must be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name/trade-mark, outside diameter, class and pressure rating, batch/lot number, and the word 'plumbing' (for plumbing pipes) at intervals of not more than 3 m. Type A water-supply pipes must also bear a continuous longitudinal blue strip.

Markings or circumferential bands must be colour-coded strictly by pipe class to prevent installation mix-ups: Class 1 (Red), Class 2 (Blue), Class 3 (Green), Class 4 (Brown), Class 5 (Yellow), Class 6 (Black), and Plumbing (Pink).

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 4985:2021 is the national standard specification in India for unplasticized polyvinyl chloride (UPVC) pressure pipes designed for drinking water distribution, plumbing, and agricultural networks. It categorizes pipes into Classes 1 through 6 based on their design working pressure rating (ranging from 0.25 to 1.25 MPa at 27 °C). Crucially, this revision introduces a strict phase-out program for lead-based stabilizers in accordance with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF & CC) guidelines, differentiating water supply (Type A, blue strip) and agricultural pipes (Type B) to manage lead stabilizer transitions. When sourcing or verifying these pipes, engineers must ensure that physical parameters (density, Vicat softening temperature, sulphated ash), VCM monomer limits, and short-term and long-term hydrostatic testing requirements are rigorously checked against manufacturer certifications.
